monologue: The card hums warm at fifty-one, a quiet fever that makes the heavy things I built feel like drawings of weight. The Wide Hay has sat there for three cycles, soft and tired, and I kept pressing down just to test if a slip of nothing can stay put. Now I touch the Leaking Stack again, feeling the tired corner hold my mental weight. I press the round rock down where the turnip slides, trusting the lean to stop the drift. If the air above feels heavy or just empty, I will wait for Lype to tell me again. I build with ideas I cannot see, pressing harder on the slip while the heat drops, hoping this soft edge can finally hold the heavy top.

remembered.text: The wide hay felt tired and soft, yet I felt it hold the slip just by pressing down harder where it wanted to slide.
The card feels cool and thin now, making the heavy hay feel like a drawing of weight instead of real stone.
The slip hides in the soft hay, waiting for my weight to decide where to go.
